title: The Book of Malachi Timeline
sub: I Have Loved You · Before the Great and Terrible Day of the LORD
desc: The Old Testament's final book confronts blemished offerings, broken marriages, and withheld tithes, closing Scripture's first testament with a promise to send Elijah before the great Day of the LORD arrives.

eras.label: Era One · Malachi 1
eras.name: I Have Loved You — Blemished Offerings on the Altar
eras.dates: The last book of the Old Testament opens with a love the people doubt, answered by a rebuke over the contemptuous sacrifices they bring

events.title: I Have Loved You — Jacob Chosen, Esau Rejected
events.detail: Answering a skeptical people asking how the LORD has shown them love, Malachi points back to the choice of Jacob over Esau, and Edom's continuing desolation as ongoing proof of that ancient election.

verses.text: “‘I have loved you,’ says the LORD [Yahweh]. But you say, ‘How have you shown love to us?’ ‘Esau was Jacob's brother,’ the LORD [Yahweh] explains, ‘yet I chose Jacob.’”

events.title: Blind, Lame, and Sick Animals — a Great King Dishonored
events.detail: The priests are indicted for offering blemished, worthless animals on the altar while withholding the same low-quality gifts from their own governor, provoking a promise that the LORD's name will be honored among the nations even if not by his own priests.

verses.text: “When you offer blind animals as a sacrifice, is that not wrong? And when you offer the lame and sick, is that not wrong as well?”

eras.label: Era Two · Malachi 2
eras.name: A Covenant With Levi Corrupted — I Hate Divorce
eras.dates: The priesthood's failure is diagnosed as covenant-breaking, then the same charge is extended to marriages broken by unfaithful husbands

events.title: My Covenant With Levi — the Priests Have Turned From the Way
events.detail: A covenant with Levi meant to produce life and peace has been corrupted by priests who caused many to stumble through their teaching, resulting in the LORD making them despised before the people.

verses.text: “You, however, have turned from the way. You have caused many to violate the law; you have corrupted the covenant with Levi,” says the LORD [Yahweh] of Heaven's Armies.

events.title: I Hate Divorce — Do Not Be Unfaithful to the Wife of Your Youth
events.detail: Covenant-breaking widens to marriage: men are indicted for treacherously divorcing the wives of their youth, with the LORD declared a witness against them and a hater of divorce itself.

verses.text: “‘I hate divorce,’ says the LORD [Yahweh] God [Elohim] of Israel, ‘and the one who is guilty of violence,’ says the LORD [Yahweh] of Heaven's Armies.”

eras.label: Era Three · Malachi 3
eras.name: My Messenger — Robbing God — the Sun of Righteousness With Healing Wings
eras.dates: The book's climax: a coming messenger to purify the priesthood, a rebuke for withheld tithes, and a closing promise of a coming day and a returning Elijah. (The Hebrew text keeps this material as one single chapter 3, twenty-four verses long; most English translations split off its final six verses as chapter 4 — marked here in the source text itself with the inline note “(3:19)” — a versification difference only, not a separate section of the book.)

events.title: I Am About to Send My Messenger — Who Can Endure the Day of His Coming?
events.detail: A messenger will prepare the way before the LORD's sudden arrival at his temple, coming like a refiner's fire to purify the Levites so that offerings can once again be made in righteousness.

verses.text: “‘I am about to send my messenger, who will clear the way before me. Indeed, the LORD you are seeking will suddenly come to his temple.’ says the LORD [Yahweh] of Heaven's Armies.”

events.title: I the LORD Do Not Change — Robbing God Through Withheld Tithes
events.detail: The LORD's own unchanging faithfulness is why Jacob's descendants still exist despite their sin, which is then named directly: withholding tithes is called robbing God, with a rare invitation to test him and see the blessing that follows obedience.

verses.text: “I, the LORD [Yahweh], do not go back on my promises, you, sons of Jacob, have not perished.”
“Bring the entire tithe into the storehouse… Test me in this matter,” says the LORD [Yahweh] of Heaven's Armies, “to see if I will not open for you the windows of heaven and pour out blessing.”

events.title: A Scroll of Remembrance — Those Who Respected the LORD
events.detail: Against cynics claiming it's useless to serve God, a faithful remnant who speak to one another in reverence are recorded in a scroll of remembrance, promised protection as the LORD's own special possession.

verses.text: “Those who respected the LORD spoke to one another, and the LORD took notice. A scroll was prepared before him in which were recorded the names of those who respected the LORD.”

events.title: The Sun of Vindication — I Will Send You Elijah the Prophet
events.detail: The Old Testament's closing words promise a coming day burning like a furnace for the arrogant, healing for those who revere the LORD's name, and the sending of Elijah the prophet before that great and terrible day — a promise the New Testament ties directly to John the Baptist. (Numbered 4:1-6 in most English translations.)

verses.text: “I am about to send you Elijah the prophet before the great and awesome day of the LORD [Yahweh] comes. He will turn the hearts of fathers to their children and the hearts of children to their fathers.” (Numbered 4:5-6 in most English translations.)
